readmeExcerpt:
Magnitude

Run open models as fast as your hardware allows

Magnitude is an open source inference engine that tunes its kernels on your hardware to find the fastest way to run each model. It's over 2x faster than Ollama and works on Apple Silicon, NVIDIA, AMD, Intel, or just a CPU. One click connects it to the agent you already use (Pi, OpenCode, Hermes, Codex, and more). ⭐ Help us reach more developers and grow the Magnitude community. Star this repo! ## Get started Magnitude comes with a desktop app and a CLI. Install from your terminal: macOS / Linux: ```sh curl -fsSL https://magnitude.dev/install.sh | sh ``` Windows PowerShell: ```powershell irm https://magnitude.dev/install.ps1 | iex ``` Or download the installer: - **macOS:** [Apple silicon](https://magnitude.dev/api/installer?os=darwin&arch=arm64&package=dmg) · [Intel](https://magnitude.dev/api/installer?os=darwin&arch=x64&package=dmg) - **Windows:** [x64](https://magnitude.dev/api/installer?os=windows&arch=x64&package=windows-exe) - **Linux x64:** [.deb](https://magnitude.dev/api/installer?os=linux&arch=x64&package=deb) · [.rpm](https://magnitude.dev/api/installer?os=linux&arch=x64&package=rpm) · [.pkg.tar.zst](https://magnitude.dev/api/installer?os=linux&arch=x64&package=pacman) - **Linux ARM64:** [.deb](https://magnitude.dev/api/installer?os=linux&arch=arm64&package=deb) · [.rpm](https://magnitude.dev/api/installer?os=linux&arch=arm64&package=rpm) To run Magnitude as a service other computers can use, see [Remote server](https://docs.magnitude.dev/remote-server). To run it in a container, see [Docker](https://docs.magnitude.dev/installation/docker). ## Why Magnitude? - **2x faster than Ollama:** on average across popular local models, on Mac and NVIDIA - **Tuned on your hardware:** kernels are tuned for each model when you download it - **Best drafter built in:** each model ships with the fastest speculative decoding drafter - **Memory that flexes:** quantized KV halves memory per agent, freed when agents stop - **Fast concurrent sessions:** sessions share prefix caches to prevent slowdown - **Works with your agent:** one click to connect Pi, OpenCode, Hermes, Codex, and more - **Free, private, open source:** no token costs, nothing leaves your machine, Apache 2.0 ## Over 2x faster than Ollama [View full benchmarks →](https://magnitude.dev/benchmarks) ## FAQ ### What is Magnitude? An open source inference engine that optimizes each model for your exact hardware. It ships as a desktop app that runs open models and connects them to the agent you already use. ### How is it faster than llama.cpp, Ollama, or LM Studio? They ship one-size-fits-all kernels, because tuning each model for each chip by hand would take forever. Magnitude tunes them automatically. When you download a model, it spends up to a minute on your actual chip trying different ways to split up the math (how many GPU threads team up, how big a chunk each one takes, how far ahead to load data) and keeps the fastest combination that doesn't change the model's output. [See the full benchmarks against Ollama.](https://magnitude.dev/benchmarks) ### What hardware do I need? Any Apple Silicon, NVIDIA, AMD, or Intel GPU, or nothing but a CPU. There is no fixed minimum. Smaller machines run smaller models, and more memory lets you run larger ones. ### What operating systems does it support? macOS, Linux, and Windows. ### Which models does it support? See the full list at [magnitude.dev/models](https://magnitude.dev/models). We write optimized kernels for the most popular open-weight families, which is how we beat generalist engines. ### Which agents work with it? One click connects Pi, OpenCode, Hermes, OpenClaw, Codex, Claude Code, Oh My Pi, and Cline. Anything else works through the OpenAI-compatible API. ### Is it private? Yes. Prompts, files, and models stay on your machine. No internet needed once a model is downloaded.
readmeHtml:
Magnitude

Run open models as fast as your hardware allows

Magnitude is an open source inference engine that tunes its kernels on your hardware to find the fastest way to run each model. It's over 2x faster than Ollama and works on Apple Silicon, NVIDIA, AMD, Intel, or just a CPU. One click connects it to the agent you already use (Pi, OpenCode, Hermes, Codex, and more).

⭐ Help us reach more developers and grow the Magnitude community. Star this repo!

Get started

Magnitude comes with a desktop app and a CLI. Install from your terminal:

macOS / Linux:

curl -fsSL https://magnitude.dev/install.sh | sh

Windows PowerShell:

irm https://magnitude.dev/install.ps1 | iex

Or download the installer:

  • macOS: Apple silicon · Intel
  • Windows: x64
  • Linux x64: .deb · .rpm · .pkg.tar.zst
  • Linux ARM64: .deb · .rpm

To run Magnitude as a service other computers can use, see Remote server. To run it in a container, see Docker.

Why Magnitude?

  • 2x faster than Ollama: on average across popular local models, on Mac and NVIDIA
  • Tuned on your hardware: kernels are tuned for each model when you download it
  • Best drafter built in: each model ships with the fastest speculative decoding drafter
  • Memory that flexes: quantized KV halves memory per agent, freed when agents stop
  • Fast concurrent sessions: sessions share prefix caches to prevent slowdown
  • Works with your agent: one click to connect Pi, OpenCode, Hermes, Codex, and more
  • Free, private, open source: no token costs, nothing leaves your machine, Apache 2.0

Over 2x faster than Ollama

View full benchmarks →

FAQ

What is Magnitude?

An open source inference engine that optimizes each model for your exact hardware. It ships as a desktop app that runs open models and connects them to the agent you already use.

How is it faster than llama.cpp, Ollama, or LM Studio?

They ship one-size-fits-all kernels, because tuning each model for each chip by hand would take forever. Magnitude tunes them automatically. When you download a model, it spends up to a minute on your actual chip trying different ways to split up the math (how many GPU threads team up, how big a chunk each one takes, how far ahead to load data) and keeps the fastest combination that doesn't change the model's output. See the full benchmarks against Ollama.

What hardware do I need?

Any Apple Silicon, NVIDIA, AMD, or Intel GPU, or nothing but a CPU. There is no fixed minimum. Smaller machines run smaller models, and more memory lets you run larger ones.

What operating systems does it support?

macOS, Linux, and Windows.

Which models does it support?

See the full list at magnitude.dev/models. We write optimized kernels for the most popular open-weight families, which is how we beat generalist engines.

Which agents work with it?

One click connects Pi, OpenCode, Hermes, OpenClaw, Codex, Claude Code, Oh My Pi, and Cline. Anything else works through the OpenAI-compatible API.

Is it private?

Yes. Prompts, files, and models stay on your machine. No internet needed once a model is downloaded.

releases.body:
## 0.2.16

### Patch Changes

- [`b4eb689`](https://github.com/magnitudedev/magnitude/commit/b4eb689ee384cfdc16fd628de0727f3044eddc7f) Thanks [@thrgreenwald](https://github.com/thrgreenwald)! - Fix concurrent chats with a shared prompt prefix unloading the model with "target state capacity changed after availability check" ([#237](https://github.com/magnitudedev/magnitude/issues/237), reported by @Wenjix). Requests that continue the same cached prefix now grow together instead of failing every request in flight.

  Concurrent requests that share a long prompt, such as an agent's parallel subagents, are also much faster:

  - A request now waits for another request that is already computing their shared prefix and reuses it, instead of computing it again. With a draft model, 8 concurrent requests sharing a 15K-token prompt went from 226 s each to 3.5 s on an NVIDIA A10G.
  - A shared prefix stays cached after a batch finishes, so repeating it is fast: 4 concurrent requests on a 13.6K-token prompt went from 12 s to 0.7 s, and 8 from 24 s to 1.2 s.
  - Long conversations running side by side recompute their history from scratch less often.

releases.body:
## 0.2.15

### Patch Changes

- [`ae7875a`](https://github.com/magnitudedev/magnitude/commit/ae7875a7b347817abce5f8efbbe8aec40d39595f) Thanks [@thrgreenwald](https://github.com/thrgreenwald)! - The inference engine's Anthropic-compatible messages and token-counting endpoints now accept any `anthropic-version` header value, or no header, instead of rejecting clients that do not send `2023-06-01`.

- [`ae7875a`](https://github.com/magnitudedev/magnitude/commit/ae7875a7b347817abce5f8efbbe8aec40d39595f) Thanks [@anerli](https://github.com/anerli)! - Fix model loading on Metal exceeding its reserved weight-import memory when streaming weight tables ([#231](https://github.com/magnitudedev/magnitude/issues/231)). Import batches now share the memory plan used to reserve their budget, accounting for mapped file spans and simultaneous staged uploads.

aiSummary.oneLiner: An open-source inference server that seamlessly connects AI coding agents to locally hosted models
aiSummary.whatItDoes: Magnitude is a localized inference server designed to bridge the gap between popular AI coding agents (like Claude Code, OpenCode, and Pi) and locally hosted language models. It acts as a smart middleware that profiles the user's host hardware, recommends the optimal models that fit within local memory constraints, and automatically handles downloading and tuning. Once running, it exposes a standardized endpoint that existing agent software can plug into seamlessly. This enables developers to use powerful, automated agent tools entirely offline and privately, without relying on costly or privacy-invasive cloud APIs.
keyFeatures: Hardware profiling: automatically analyzes system resources to recommend models that fit within available RAM and VRAM.
Seamless agent integration: provides drop-in compatibility with popular coding agents like Claude Code, OpenClaw, and Hermes.
Automated model management: handles the downloading, tuning, and execution of local models without manual configuration.
Offline execution: ensures all inference and data processing stays entirely on the local machine for maximum privacy.
Standardized API endpoint: exposes a uniform interface that mimics cloud providers, allowing existing tools to connect without modification.

useCases.title: Private Code Generation
useCases.description: Allows enterprise developers to use AI coding assistants on proprietary codebases without sending sensitive data to external cloud providers.

useCases.title: Offline Development
useCases.description: Enables engineers to utilize powerful AI agents while working on air-gapped systems or during travel without internet access.

useCases.title: Cost Reduction
useCases.description: Helps heavy users of AI coding tools avoid mounting API costs by shifting inference workloads to their local hardware.

useCases.title: Local Model Experimentation
useCases.description: Provides a streamlined way for developers to test how different open-source models perform with their preferred agent workflows.

aiSummary.whoIsItFor: Magnitude is built for software engineers, security-conscious organizations, and AI enthusiasts who want to leverage modern AI coding agents using their own hardware. It is ideal for users with capable local machines who prioritize data privacy and zero-cost inference.
